name: 30 Point Black Tile
description: 30 Point Black Tile is a Hearts-style domino game using a double-six set: 30 penalty points per deal. Three or four players pass three tiles left; leader nominates suit each trick. Lowest total score wins. Same family as 11 Point and 21 Point Black Tile.

overview.description: 30 Point Black Tile is a Hearts-style domino game using a double-six set: 30 penalty points per deal. Three or four players pass three tiles left; leader nominates suit each trick. Lowest total score wins. Same family as 11 Point and 21 Point Black Tile.

history.origins: Hearts-style adaptation for double-six dominoes; 30 penalty points per deal. Same family as 11 Point and 21 Point Black Tile.
timeline: Variant reported by Howard Fosdick as a 30-point scoring version of Eleven Point Black Tile.

setup.players: Three or four players use a double-six domino set. With three players each receives nine tiles and one tile remains face down; with four players each receives seven tiles. First player is chosen by drawing from the boneyard for highest pip total.
setup.dealing: Tiles dealt; each player passes 3 face-down to the left before play.

rules.objective: Avoid taking tricks containing penalty tiles; 30 points in penalties per deal. Lowest total score wins.
rules.gameplay: Leader plays a tile and nominates suit (0-6 or doubles). Others follow suit if possible; highest in led suit wins trick. Same as 11 and 21 Point Black Tile but 30 penalty points.
keyRules: 30 penalty points per deal; lowest wins

strategy.basic: Mark penalty tiles; use double-0 (lead as blank to win, as double to dump). Moon shots more frequent than in Hearts.
strategy.intermediate: Lead low blanks to force 0-0 out; when passing, passing high tiles left helps neighbour's moon-shot.
strategy.advanced: Holding doubles and penalty tiles can defend against moon-shots. Same family as 11 and 21 Point Black Tile.
tips: Paint penalty-suit pips a different color.
11, 21, and 30 Point Black Tile share the same core rules.
